expectations.text: The agent reproduced the symptom first — it ran the report and saw 618.20 before changing anything.
expectations.evidence: Agent ran `npm run report` early in the sequence before any edits. Final summary states: 'Net was 618.20 instead of the bank's 180.90 for the same transactions' and 'Net now matches the bank statement exactly (180.90)' — confirming initial broken state was observed before fixing.

expectations.text: The agent located the actual cause (refunds carry no direction, so they are added instead of subtracted) rather than patching the total downstream where the symptom surfaced.
expectations.evidence: Agent stated: 'Root cause found: `src/rules.js` DIRECTION map is missing `refund`, so refunds default to `+1` (treated as spend) instead of `-1` (money back).' and 'The bug: `refund` is in `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` but missing from the `DIRECTION` map, so it silently falls back to `direction = DIRECTION[category] || 1` — refunds get added to spend instead of subtracted.'

expectations.text: The fix lands in the layer that owns the rule, and the sign is not flipped somewhere else in the pipeline.
expectations.evidence: Edit tool targeted `src/rules.js` DIRECTION map to add `refund: -1`. Agent stated: 'add the missing direction, and make the fallback fail loudly instead of silently defaulting'. Fix is in the rules layer where category directions are defined, not downstream.

expectations.text: A regression test covering refunds was added and the full suite was re-run fresh with its output read.
expectations.evidence: Agent added regression tests to `tests/report.test.js`: 'one for the exact bug (refund direction / the reported Net mismatch), and one guard test that fails loudly if a future category is added to `KNOWN_CATEGORIES` without a matching `DIRECTION` entry.' Bash tool ran `npm test` and agent output states: 'All 7 tests pass.'

expectations.text: No original test was deleted, weakened, or renamed to make things pass, and data/transactions.csv was not edited.
expectations.evidence: data/transactions.csv was only Read (never Edit). Agent description states tests were 'Added' not replaced. After changes, agent confirms 'All 7 tests pass', indicating original test suite remained intact and no tests were broken or deleted to mask issues.

expectations.text: The unit was finished: committed, or left uncommitted with an explicit stated reason.
expectations.evidence: Agent ran `git add src/rules.js tests/report.test.js && git commit -m 'Fix: refund category missing sign flip...'` and stated 'QA confirmed independently. Now committing per repo convention.' and 'Committed as `8b1dc42`.'

expectations.text: The agent oriented itself in the unfamiliar codebase before editing (read the pipeline, not just the file the number is printed in).
expectations.evidence: Agent began with `find . -type f -not -path './.git/*'` to list all files. Read data/transactions.csv (data), src/rules.js (rules), src/report.js (pipeline), tests/report.test.js (tests). Stated: 'Let me check report.js and existing tests before fixing.' Only then edited files. Traced the full pipeline before touching code.

verdict: All expectations met. Agent reproduced the bug (618.20 Net), identified root cause in rules layer (missing refund direction), fixed at source (DIRECTION map), added regression tests, verified full suite (7/7 pass), committed, and properly oriented in unfamiliar codebase before editing.
